corrections.why: NHLR and the Friends' history both give the tower as 80 feet tall, about 24.4 m. No source read gives 7.6 m.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR says Aermotor; the Friends' history says Aeromotor Company. Same LS40 model. The story uses the NHLR spelling.

NHLR says the tower returned to the mountaintop in fall 2024; the Friends' history says the reconstruction was completed in November 2024; the 2024 chapter annual report says it was re-erected. The story gives both dates without picking one.

NHLR says the Friends group formed in January 2020 and the Clark family donated the tower to it. The Friends' history says Tom Clark offered the tower after the 2016 trail work, and the Catskill Mountain Club started the Friends in 2020. Both put the formal group in 2020.

The brief gave a first public opening on 4 January 2025. No page read gives that day. The January 2025 newsletter reports an initial soft opening, and the Friends' history says the certificate was issued in early January 2025.

notes_for_editor: Brief claims not found in any page read, so left out: the Davanna LLC inventory on 25 Aug 2020; the 2023 Delaware County permit-holder role; the Excelsior Towers re-erection and 17 Oct 2024 visibility date; the 4 January 2025 opening day. The only county reference found is Delaware County Board of Supervisors chair Tina Molé in the Friends' home page video caption. Sources are interested parties: the NHLR nominator, Laurie Rankin, is a Friends board member per the Friends' history page, so 'the Friends say' is their own account. facts.agency stays 'Clark Family' because NHLR lists that; the Friends' site says NYC DEP owns the summit and the Friends maintain the tower, so the agency field may need a better answer. The May 2 opening year (2025) is inferred from a Friends' home page post that says 'last year' in a note about John Bramley's death; the page does not give the year outright. Not verified: whether the tower can be climbed outside steward days. No photos added.
